remediation.fix_approach: Added MAX_FIELDS = 10000 constant to ScreenProcessorService. filterCollisions() checks fields.length against MAX_FIELDS at the start of each iteration and breaks if exceeded. Replaced fields.concat([f1, f2]) with split.forEach(f => fields.push(f)) for O(1) amortized append instead of O(n) allocation per split.
remediation.root_cause: filterCollisions() used fields = fields.concat(this.splitField(field, rect)) which allocates a new array on every split, causing O(n) allocation per collision and O(n²) total. A crafted ApplinX REST response with 1000 overlapping transformation rectangles could cause ~500K iterations and ~1GB memory allocation, freezing the browser tab for 10-60 seconds.
changes_made: src/app/services/screen-processor.service.ts filterCollisions(): added fields.length > MAX_FIELDS guard with break and console.warn
src/app/services/screen-processor.service.ts filterCollisions(): replaced fields.concat() with split.forEach(f => fields.push(f))
src/app/services/screen-processor.service.ts filterCollisions(): renamed inner loop variable from i to j to avoid shadowing
remediation.verification_needed: Test screen rendering with a normal screen (< 100 fields). Verify truncation console.warn appears when a malformed test response exceeds 10000 fields.
remediation.defense_in_depth: VULN-006 optional chaining fix also applied — even if MAX_FIELDS is reached with a null-content field, the crash is avoided.
remediation.testing: Unit test: generate fields array with 10001 elements — verify filterCollisions returns without hanging. Verify normal 100-field screen renders correctly.
remediation.residual_risk: Low. 10000 fields is approximately 100x the maximum seen in real ApplinX screens (typical: 50-300 fields). The limit can be raised if legitimate screens approach it.
